---
title: "A Comparison of Neural Recommender System Architectures"
description: "An independent study of neural recommender architectures, hyperparameter search, and optimization under a common computational budget."
---

::: {.project-intro}
This independent study asks whether increased model and optimization complexity improves recommendation-style edge prediction when architectures, search methods, and optimizers are evaluated under a shared, constrained model-search budget.

[Explore the repository ↗](https://github.com/Kaxlow/rec-sys-nn-optimization){.btn .btn-primary}
[Read the draft manuscript ↗](https://github.com/Kaxlow/rec-sys-nn-optimization/tree/main/paper){.btn .btn-outline-primary}
:::

## Three comparisons

1. **Architecture:** six model families spanning embedding, graph, sequential, relational-feature, and policy-guided approaches.
2. **Hyperparameter search:** grid, random, and Differential Evolution-style search, each with 24 candidate evaluations over the same search domain.
3. **Optimization:** Adam and momentum SGD compared with particle swarm and evolution-strategy-style methods.

## Making the comparison meaningful

Each method uses the same five trial seeds. Hyperparameters are selected by mean validation AUC, then the selected configuration is retrained and evaluated on the test split. Candidate-search rows contain no test results, keeping the test set out of model selection.

Alongside ROC AUC and average precision, the harness records time and resource use. The aim is to compare predictive performance with the computational cost of obtaining it.

## Evaluation datasets

The experiments are evaluated using two common benchmark datasets: the MovieLens 100K dataset which contains user-movie ratings, and the Open Graph Benchmark's `ogbl-collab` dataset which is a large, undirected graph representing a network of author collaborations. The main purpose of the smaller MovieLens 100K dataset is to validate that the proposed model candidates work as expected, while the larger `ogbl-collab` dataset is used to assess their performance on a more complex link-prediction task. The MovieLens 100K dataset is transformed into a user–item graph of positive interactions.

## Results

The August 25, 2026 run used one NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU. These are mean test ROC AUC values ± sample standard deviation over five seeds, as [reported in the repository](https://github.com/Kaxlow/rec-sys-nn-optimization#current-repeated-trial-results).

| Comparison | MovieLens 100K | ogbl-collab |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Highest mean AUC, model families | DNN: **0.4627 ± 0.0096** | PSL-DNN: **0.9477 ± 0.0015** |
| Highest mean AUC, search methods | Grid: **0.6562 ± 0.0183** | DE-style: **0.9178 ± 0.0051** |
| Highest mean AUC, optimizers | PSO: **0.5107 ± 0.0288** | Adam: **0.8650 ± 0.0243** |

The weak MovieLens model-family results are part of the story: the strongest default family in that comparison still scored below 0.5 AUC. Tuning results were better, but the three MovieLens search methods remained close, from 0.6528 to 0.6562.

On `ogbl-collab`, DE-style search had the highest mean test AUC, while grid search had the lowest measured candidate-search time. These are descriptive comparisons, not formal significance tests.

## What I built

A shared PyTorch experiment harness, repeatable dataset preparation and negative sampling, validation-only hyperparameter selection, resource measurements, and separate result files for CPU quick-mode and full-data GPU runs. The repository also includes tests, a notebook that runs the experiments and shows the results, a GPU batch script, and the manuscript.

::: {.callout-note}
## Notes

- The manuscript is an unpublished working draft that has not been formally peer reviewed
- Hybrid models are compact research approximations rather than full reproductions of the architectures that inspired them
:::
